messages:
maria: Heads up — since last Thursday we've had intermittent streaming token stalls for hosted streams in us-west-2. Symptoms: long gaps between tokens and occasional gRPC errors (DeadlineExceeded). Looks correlated with packet reordering / jitter on pod-to-pod paths. cc @jay @liu

jay: Can you paste a short example and any perf numbers?

maria: Short log: `rpc: stream error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded`
Reorder metric from packet-capture job: `reorder_pct=0.92%` (baseline ~0.02%). p99 inter-packet gap for token stream TCP conn = 150ms (baseline 12ms).

maria: tcpdump excerpt (trimmed):
```
12:01:02.123456 IP pod-a.53820 > pod-b.17001: Seq=1001 Ack=2001 Len=120
12:01:02.123457 IP pod-a.53820 > pod-b.17001: Seq=881  Ack=2001 Len=120  # out-of-order
12:01:02.123458 IP pod-a.53820 > pod-b.17001: Seq=1121 Ack=2001 Len=200
```

anika: Is this cross-AZ traffic or same-AZ? Could be fabric path difference.

maria: Mostly same-AZ, different racks / ToRs. We started seeing spikes after last week's kube-proxy iptables->ipvs rollout to the dedicated pool.

sam: Quick thought: when RDMA/GPUDirect was enabled in a different cluster we saw similar visible reordering when flows hit mixed RDMA/TCP paths. Are any nodes toggling RDMA or NIC offloads?

liu: Two common causes: ECMP/LAG hashing sending segments out-of-order across parallel paths, or NIC offloads (GRO/LRO/GSO/TSO) + kernel batching exposing reordering on capture. MTU mismatch can also create fragmentation-induced reordering.

maria: Checked MTU across nodes: `ip link show` shows 9000 everywhere. ToR firmware diffs: some racks on 1.2.15 vs 1.2.8.

jay: Can we reproduce with iperf3/udp or tcpreplay between the offending pod pairs? Run two things: 1) measure reorder/jitter with `iperf3 -u` and 2) capture with `tcpdump -U -w` to get real ordering. Also try disabling offloads on one host to see immediate effect: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`

maria: Did a quick test on one canary node: after disabling GRO/GSO/TSO reorder_pct dropped from 0.9% -> 0.03% and the streaming gaps vanished for that node pool.

sam: That matches our past findings. Disabling host-side GRO/LRO reduces kernel coalescing that can make user-space see reorders for small TCP segments used by token streaming.

liu: Longer term: vendor asked us to collect pcap + ToR counters for ECMP skew. We'll open a ticket. In parallel we should:
- Roll back kube-proxy ipvs change on the dedicated pool as a quick A/B (if kube-proxy is implicated)
- Test a GRO-off node pool as a mitigation while networking team investigates
- Tune gRPC timeouts for streaming to be more robust to occasional jitter (increase deadline by 50ms for now)

anika: Cost/ops note: disabling offloads increases CPU on host NIC processing. We should limit canary to a small node group. Estimate +5-7% CPU for streaming-heavy boxes.

jay: Plan for next 48h: 1) small canary (10 nodes) with `ethtool -K ... gro off gso off tso off` (owner: maria) 2) roll back ipvs in the dedicated pool to prior snapshot (owner: jay) 3) network vendor ticket with pcaps and ToR diffs (owner: liu) 4) temporary increase to stream deadlines (owner: sam)

maria: Starting canary now. I'll post results in ~3h. If anyone sees other affected regions, ping here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

liu: I'll gather ToR logs and counters and request vendor support.

sam: In case we need an immediate app-level patch, we can buffer tokens slightly and emit keepalive frames to avoid deadline tripping while we fix infra. Not ideal but doable as fallback.

anika: Sounds good — keep it small. Add cost hit estimate to the canary ticket. :+1:
